title: Coherent conjugation gives functorial Hom transitions
statement:
Let $I$ be a preordered set, $\mathcal C_i$ categories [def-nagata-category], $T_{ij}:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ functors for $i\le j$, and $\tau_{ijk}:T_{jk}T_{ij}\cong T_{ik}$ natural isomorphisms. Assume $T_{ii}=\mathrm{Id}$, $\tau_{iij}=\tau_{ijj}=\mathrm{id}$ and, for $i\le j\le k\le l$,
$$\tau_{ikl}\circ T_{kl}(\tau_{ijk})=\tau_{ijl}\circ(\tau_{jkl})_{T_{ij}}.$$
For labels $a=(i,x)$, $b=(j,y)$ put $H_k(a,b)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_k}(T_{ik}x,T_{jk}y)$ when $k\ge i,j$, and define
$$t^{ab}_{kn}(g)=\tau_{jkn,y}\circ T_{kn}(g)\circ\tau_{ikn,x}^{-1}\quad(k\le n).$$
Then $t^{ab}_{kk}=\mathrm{id}$ and $t^{ab}_{np}t^{ab}_{kn}=t^{ab}_{kp}$ for all admissible $k\le n\le p$. More explicitly, writing $A_{a;k,n}=\tau_{ikn,x}$, the endpoint identity
$$A_{a;n,p}T_{np}(A_{a;k,n})=A_{a;k,p}\tau_{knp,T_{ik}x}$$
holds (and likewise for $b$), and the resulting composite is
$$t^{ab}_{np}(t^{ab}_{kn}g)=A_{b;k,p}\tau_{knp,T_{jk}y}T_{np}T_{kn}(g)\tau_{knp,T_{ik}x}^{-1}A_{a;k,p}^{-1}=A_{b;k,p}T_{kp}(g)A_{a;k,p}^{-1}.$$
For three labels $a,b,c$, whenever all their indices are at most $k\le n$, the transitions preserve the stage products and identities:
$$t^{ac}_{kn}(h\circ g)=t^{bc}_{kn}(h)\circ t^{ab}_{kn}(g),\qquad t^{aa}_{kn}(\mathrm{id}_{T_{ik}x})=\mathrm{id}_{T_{in}x}.$$
In particular each pair gives a diagram of sets on its common-stage preorder. No directedness or cocone vertex is required.
